`data-vd-split` (chars/words/lines; pieces inherit the motion minus `stagger`).

**`presets` is one of those modules, not a built-in list.** `wireDirectives([motion, presets])`
wires the ten shipped names; without it a preset name is refused as unwired rather than misspelled.
**A preset is a motion value with a name** — the same shape as the attribute, `keyframes` plus any
settings — so a pack can encode a whole house style under one word. The expansion runs BEFORE every
other key, so an explicit key always wins whichever order it is written in.

`presets` is a DUAL, like `motion` and `sequence`: bare for the shipped ten, called for your own.
**`presets(table)` MERGES over the shipped ten**, key by key, yours winning — so overriding one name
keeps the other nine, and it builds the `hasOwnProperty` lookup for you (a bare `TABLE[name]`
resolves `"constructor"` to `Object.prototype.constructor`). Wire ONE of them: the insert chain
answers from the first resolver, so wiring both means the shipped table answers and your overrides
silently do not apply — refused as `motion-presets-wired-twice`. To inherit nothing, use
`motionExtension({ on: 'preset', fn })`, which never references the shipped table and drops it from
the bundle. `motionExtension` is also how a module adds animatable PROPERTIES (`{ key, category,
… }`), SETTINGS (`{ key, type, … }`) or hooks an insert point (`preset`, `easing`, `prepare`,
`release`, `teardown`, `forget`) — keys REPLACE with a warning, inserts CHAIN.

**remote pack** — `data-vd-fetch="{ url, on, into, place, body, method, status, debounce, animate }"`.
`debounce: 250` holds the request until the trigger is quiet that long (the wire waits; the
local state write stays instant). **The response
decides**: JSON is a state patch (existing reflections update themselves), anything else is markup
swapped into `into` — and swapped markup is live immediately, because directives are never
hydrated. Same-origin by default (`remote({ allowedOrigins, headers })` is the only way to widen,
and it is JavaScript, never an attribute); **markup is swapped same-origin ONLY, always**. A later
request aborts an earlier one. `place: 'append' | 'prepend'` accumulates into the target instead
of replacing it (existing DOM is parsed around, never rewritten — state and handlers survive);
omit it for replace. `animate: true` morphs the swap old-to-new through
`startViewTransition` (the flip door `list` uses — same guards: `on: 'load'` never animates, no
support or reduced-motion degrade to the instant swap).

**sensors, the sugar tier**: `data-vd-in-view` also DISPATCHES `vera:in-view` (bubbling,
`detail.visible`) on every transition — the trigger surface: infinite scroll is a sentinel
`<div data-vd-in-view="near" data-vd-fetch="{ url: …, on: 'vera:in-view', place: 'append' }">`,
three existing pieces composing for real. `data-vd-in-view="seen:once"` latches (a reveal is not
un-revealed); `"reveal:down"` is a directional latch — only a downward exit (the reader going
back up) resets, so the reveal replays coming down; `data-vd-size="s:viewport"` writes the WINDOW's size — breakpoints
are ordinary expressions (`data-vd-show="s.width < 768"`), no band vocabulary to learn;
`data-vd-pointer="p:viewport"` measures the
whole viewport (the ambient form — `sensors({ pointer: 'p' })` sets exactly that attribute on
body from JavaScript); `data-vd-in-view="toc:current"` on each section holds an election — the one
MOST in view wins, its id written to the shared key (`''` when none) — nav highlighting is `data-vd-class="{ active:
toc == 'intro' }"`. `data-vd-copy` takes `data-vd-copy-done="copied"`, a key written true on
success and self-clearing 2s later — the badge is `data-vd-show="copied"`.

**`data-vd-stream="{ url, into, event, send, status, animate }"`** — the live half of the
remote pack: a connection held open, each pushed message obeying fetch's law (JSON object =
state patch, `_vd` reserved; anything else = markup swapped into `into`, same-origin ONLY,
absolute). The URL's scheme picks the transport: `http(s)` is an EventSource (the platform
reconnects it), `ws(s)` a WebSocket (the pack reconnects it, capped backoff). Connections are
shared per URL. `event: 'score'` listens to named SSE events (space/comma list; default
`message`). On a socket, `send: 'outbox'` transmits every NEW write of that state key
(JSON-serialized, queued until open, deduped by wire form; a pre-seeded outbox is establishment
and never sends). `status` writes `connecting`/`open`/`error`. Same-origin unless the origin is
in `remote({ allowedOrigins })` (`wss://site` counts as `https://site` — one authority). No SSR
half, deliberately: the page's own server render is the establishment; the stream takes over.

**query pack** — `data-vd-route` publishes `@route` (`path`, `query`, `hash`; a repeated query
key walks as an ARRAY — `@route.query.tag` is every value) · `data-vd-query="q
page"` binds state keys to the URL query string, and the URL WINS at activation so a shared link
reproduces what the sender saw · `data-vd-list` filters, sorts and paginates the items ALREADY
INSIDE it. `list` renders nothing and templates nothing: the server sends the list, the directive
writes `hidden` (and, under `sort`, reorders the server's own nodes). There is no `each` — client
templating is the renderer's job.

`data-vd-list` config (every value names a STATE key; item data lives in `data-*` attributes):
`items` (selector, default: children) · `search` (needle key; `fields` narrows to named
`data-*` fields) · `facets: 'tag'` (state `tag` matches `data-tag`; an ARRAY value is a
multi-select — any listed value matches, empty array is no filter) · `ranges: 'price'` (flat keys
`price-min`/`price-max` bound numeric `data-price`; an unset bound is no bound) · `sort: 's'`
(state `s` holds `'price'` or `'price desc'`; numeric when both sides parse, else localeCompare,
missing-attribute last; clearing the spec restores the server order) · `page`/`size`/`counts`
(counts publishes `{ matched, pages, page, total }`). · `animate: true` — reorders
and filter changes run through the platform's FLIP (`startViewTransition`) where it exists;
DISCRETE changes only (facets, sort, page — typing never animates), transient `vm-fx-*`
view-transition-names on exactly the items that change, reduced-motion skips the wrap, and the
floor everywhere else is today's instant behavior. Tune it with ordinary CSS on the
`::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements.

**Easings**: keywords, `cubic-bezier()` (x clamped 0..1), `steps()` — and `spring` /
`spring(<bounce 0..0.95>)`, OURS not CSS's: generation synthesizes it to `linear()` control
points, emitted as a fallback PAIR (`ease-out` first) so an engine without linear() keeps a
curve. `inertia-ease` refuses springs (v1 — its curve writes inline, where the pair has nowhere
to live).

`data-vd-sync` follows the native form model: text → string · bare checkbox → boolean · checkbox
WITH `value` → membership in an array key (the multi-facet shape) · radio → its `value` when
checked · `<select multiple>` (or any control whose `type` is `select-multiple`, e.g.
`<vera-select multi>`) → the whole array. State seeds may hold array literals — `{ tags: ['a'] }`
(literals only in the base grammar; the expressions tier evaluates entries). `data-vd-query`
round-trips arrays as SORTED repeated params (`?tag=css&tag=js` — the same shape a no-JS
`<form method="get">` submits, and sorted so equal filter sets are equal URLs) and restores the
SHAPE the seed declares. Readers are liberal: comma-joined (`?tags=a,b`) and PHP-style
`?tags[]=a&tags[]=b` links seed the same array. Keep a FEED's depth out of `data-vd-query` — an
accumulating view's middle pages are DOM, not URL, so a shared link would open with holes; share
an item fragment or a server cursor instead (the engine warns about this pun in development).

<!-- recipe -->
```js
import { wire } from '@verajs/core';
import { wireDirectives, directives, interactions, expressions, query, settled } from '@verajs/directives';

wire([directives]);
wireDirectives([expressions, ...interactions, query]);

/**
 * A filterable, paginated, SHAREABLE list — and the markup is complete without JavaScript:
 * the items are already here, so the page reads and indexes with the engine absent.
 * `data-vd-query` keeps `q` and `page` in the URL, so this view is a link.
 */
document.body.innerHTML = `
  <div data-vd-state="{ q: '', page: 1, counts: {} }" data-vd-query="q page">
    <input data-vd-sync="q" placeholder="filter" />
    <ul data-vd-list="{ items: 'li', search: 'q', page: 'page', size: 2, counts: 'counts' }">
      <li data-tag="fruit">apple</li>
      <li data-tag="fruit">banana</li>
      <li data-tag="tool">chisel</li>
    </ul>
    <p data-vd-text="counts.matched"></p>
    <button data-vd-on-click="{ page: page + 1 }" data-vd-show="page < counts.pages">next</button>
  </div>`;

await settled();
console.log(document.querySelectorAll('li:not([hidden])').length, 'shown of 3');
```

## CDN / buildless

```html
<script type="importmap">
  { "imports": {
      "@verajs/core":     "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/core/dist/vera.min.js",
      "@verajs/renderer": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/renderer/dist/vera-renderer.min.js",
      "@verajs/router":   "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/router/dist/vera-router.min.js" } }
</script>
```

⚠️ **Standalone bundles each inline their own copy of the insert registry**, so loading two of them
would give you two registries if any module carried one. None do — hand the router core's:

```js
import { wire } from '@verajs/core';
import { router } from '@verajs/router';
wire([router]);
```

Identical under a bundler. Order does not matter, and without core at all the router takes what it
needs directly (`setRouterRenderer`), with no registry involved.

Unnecessary under a bundler, where everything resolves to one instance. This is deliberate — it is
the price of the modules being genuinely independent of core.

---

## Buildless JSX — the whole recipe

For CodePen, a demo or a single-file app. Copy this shape; it works with no toolchain at all.

```html
<!-- Every entry is required, for two different reasons. The transform AUTO-INJECTS what a block
     uses: `html` always, plus `keyed` for `key={…}`, `spread` for `{...rest}`, and `svg`/`mathml`
     for expressions inside `<svg>`/`<math>`. The last two come from `@verajs/core`, already mapped;
     the other two are SUBPATHS, and mapping `@verajs/renderer` alone does not cover them — the page
     fails at import time with "Failed to resolve module specifier". The plain `@verajs/renderer`
     entry is for the `import { renderer }` below, which you write yourself; an explicit `keyed(…)`
     call is not auto-injected either — import it, as this block does. -->
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "@verajs/core":     "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/core@0.3.1/dist/vera.min.js",
    "@verajs/renderer": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/renderer@0.2.2/dist/vera-renderer.min.js",
    "@verajs/renderer/keyed": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/renderer@0.2.2/dist/vera-renderer-keyed.min.js",
    "@verajs/renderer/spread": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/renderer@0.2.2/dist/vera-renderer-spread.min.js"
} }
</script>

<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@verajs/jsx@0.3.2/dist/vera-jsx-standalone.min.js"></script>

<my-app></my-app>

<script type="text/vera-jsx">
  import { init, createStore, render, wire } from '@verajs/core';
  import { renderer } from '@verajs/renderer';   // the MODULE. `render` is the function it registers.
  import { keyed } from '@verajs/renderer/keyed';
  wire([renderer]);

  const state = createStore({ n: 0 });

  /* Function components are TEMPLATE FACTORIES, not custom elements.
     <Row a={x}>kid</Row> compiles to Row({ a: x, children: ["kid"] }). */
  const Row = ({ label, onPick }) => <li onClick={onPick}>{label}</li>;

  /* A real child COMPONENT. On a dash-named tag a bare prop is a PROP: `count={state.n}` below
     compiles to `.count=${state.n}`, arrives by identity, and is adopted reactively — nothing
     declared here, and the parent's next render updates it. */
  class TallyBadge extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() {
      init(this, { mode: 'open' });
      render(() => <b>picked: {String(this.count)}</b>);
    }
  }
  customElements.define('tally-badge', TallyBadge);

  class MyApp extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() {
      init(this);                       // light DOM; init(this, { mode: 'open' }) for shadow
      render(() => (
        <ul>
          {[1, 2, 3].map((i) => keyed(i, <Row label={`row ${i}`} onPick={() => state.n = i} />))}
          <tally-badge count={state.n} />
        </ul>
      ));
    }
  }
  customElements.define('my-app', MyApp);
</script>
```

**Why it works.** `standalone.js` finds every `script[type="text/vera-jsx"]` on `DOMContentLoaded`,
runs the same zero-dependency transform the Vite plugin uses, and imports the result as a module
blob. Bare specifiers inside resolve through the page's import map.

**Rules that trip up generators, in order of how often they bite:**

1. **Both import-map entries.** `@verajs/core` alone is not enough — any `key={}` emits `keyed()`
   from `@verajs/renderer/keyed`.
2. **One block is one module.** Static imports hoist, so `wire([renderer])` at the top of the
   block runs before any `customElements.define` below it. The "define before wiring" hazard
   only applies across separate files.
3. **Function components are not elements.** They compile to plain calls returning templates.
   Children arrive as `props.children`, an **array**. No hooks-in-function-components; state lives
   in a store and reactivity comes from the `render()` call in the custom element.
4. **`style` must be a string.** `style={{color:'red'}}` is a compile error; use
   `` style={`color:${c}`} ``.
5. **`{...props}` works on an element and on a component.** On an element it compiles to
   `${spread(props)}` from `@verajs/renderer/spread`, so that specifier needs an import-map entry
   too; on a component the props are passed through as an object.
6. **JS + JSX only.** Nothing strips TypeScript types in the browser; TSX needs the build path.
7. **Prefer stable shapes over conditional swaps** — see the renderer section. Toggling `hidden`
   keeps template identity and skips the clear/insert churn.
8. **Reach for `hidden={…}`, not `?hidden=${…}`, inside JSX.** On an HTML tag a bound boolean
   attribute compiles to the `?attr` form for you; on a component tag it is a prop like any other
   (`.hidden=${…}` — the platform accessor reflects it, so the element still hides).
9. **A custom element is written as itself** — `<my-comp foo={x}>…</my-comp>`, dashes and all. It is
   markup, not a function component, so it compiles into the template's statics rather than into a
   call. (Dashed tags did not parse before 0.2.0 and were emitted verbatim, which failed at load.)
10. **On a component tag, a bare prop is a PROP — React's own semantics.**
    `<x-rows rows={data} count={3} active>` passes `rows`, `count` and `active` (`true`) as
    properties, by identity: the component reads `this.rows` reactively with nothing declared, and
    SSR delivers the same props to the child's server render. The exceptions are derivations, not
    a vocabulary: names that cannot be JS identifiers (`data-*`, `aria-*`, `xlink:href`) have no
    property spelling by construction,
    and `class`/`for` — the two names the DOM itself renamed — stay attributes (write `className`,
    as in React). None of the HTML-control guesses apply on components: `disabled={x}` is the
    component's own prop, never a `?disabled` toggle. Platform names still behave: `title`, `id`,
    `slot`, `style` land on the platform accessor that owns them and reflect as always. All four
    renderer sigils (`.prop=`, `?bool=`, `@event=`, `&ref=`) also work in JSX and are passed
    through untouched — spell one when you want a specific binding, e.g. `?bool` to toggle a real
    attribute on a component for CSS. On an HTML tag, `rows={data}` is still an attribute, and the
    renderer names any non-primitive reaching an attribute sink in development.
11. **A name the mapping does not know is written verbatim**, so spell HTML attributes the way HTML
    does — `xlink:href`, not `xlinkHref`. Only `className`→`class` and `htmlFor`→`for` are renamed.
12. **Self-closing is JSX's syntax, not HTML's, and the compiler normalises both directions.**
    `<div />` emits `<div></div>` and `<br></br>` emits `<br />`, because in HTML the ELEMENT decides
    how its tag closes. Written through unchanged — as they were before 2026-09 — `<div/><span>x</span>`
    parsed to `<div><span>x</span></div>` (the sibling swallowed) and `<br></br>` rendered two breaks.
    Neither failed anywhere: server and client agreed, and only the tree was wrong. A **hand-written**
    `html` template has the identical hazard with no compiler in front of it, so `@verajs/renderer`
    warns about both in development. Children inside a void element (`<input>{label}</input>`) are
    refused outright — no markup expresses it, and passed through the binding silently left the
    element it was written inside.
13. **`key` and `ref` work on a runtime `tag` component exactly as on a written element**
    (`<H key={id} ref={r}>`), but `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` does not and cannot: a tag binds through
    `@verajs/renderer/spread`, whose names arrive at runtime, so it refuses `.innerHTML` rather than
    open a sink nothing can review. Write that element directly.

**Testing one of these without a browser:** import `transformJsx` from `@verajs/jsx`, compile the
block, and run it under jsdom with `pretendToBeVisual: true` (the default render scheduler is
`requestAnimationFrame`, so tests must await a frame). If the app uses `Math.random`, seed it —
DOM-shape-dependent bugs are otherwise intermittent and will waste your time.

---

## Server-side rendering (`@verajs/ssr`) — Node only

Vera-native, zero dependencies (no parse5, no jsdom, no lit). Components render to **declarative
shadow DOM**; `@verajs/renderer/hydrate` adopts the markup client-side.

```js
import { renderToString } from '@verajs/ssr';   // import BEFORE anything importing @verajs/renderer
const { html, styles, title } = await renderToString(new URL('./app.js', import.meta.url), options);
```

| Option | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `tag` | which element to render when the module defines several; otherwise the exported class is matched against the registry |
| `attributes` | entry tag's attributes. **An object — values escaped, names validated.** A string is written through raw |
| `props` | structured data, assigned before `connectedCallback` (an attribute can only carry a string). `__proto__` is skipped |
| `children` | markup placed inside the entry tag — what a `<slot>` renders. **Raw markup; sanitize anything from a request** |
| `location` | this request's URL. Pass it — never assign `globalThis.location` yourself; concurrent renders would race |
| `seen` | a `Set` carried across renders so shared components' styles reach a multi-island page once |
| `base` | a directory the module URL must resolve inside. Pass it whenever any part of `url` came from a request |
| `static` | `true` = stores need not be reactive: ~3x faster, identical markup. A store *write* during such a render throws in development |

Rules an assistant must not guess around:

- **Import order:** `@verajs/ssr` installs the DOM shims, so import it before any module that
  imports `@verajs/renderer` (which needs a DOM at import time).
- **`renderToString` is synchronous end to end** and refuses an `async connectedCallback` (its
  markup would be empty). **`renderToStringAsync`** (same options) awaits the lifecycle and lets
  promises settle between frame rounds — use it for async setup and for a routed component to
  render its route into the first response. Renders take a turn each: both entry points queue, so
  concurrent calls cannot read each other's in-flight state.
- **A component that throws rejects the render** — it is never silently empty markup. Catch and
  fall back to a client-rendered shell.
- `keyed()`/`hold()` are client-renderer constructs — templates that must also server-render use
  plain `.map`. `document.title` set during the render comes back as `title`.
- Escaping is at the render boundary, always; `<style>`/`<script>` contents get end-tag
  neutralisation instead (references are not decoded there). `registry` (tag → class seen by
  `customElements.define`) and `serializeTemplate` (the template flattener) are exported for
  advanced integration.
- Full semantics, limits and the measured out-of-scope list: `packages/ssr/README.md`.

---

## Not supported

Say so rather than inventing an API:

- **JSX/TSX is opt-in, never a requirement.** `@verajs/jsx` compiles JSX into the same tagged
  templates (`onClick`→`@click`, `className`→`class`, `value`→`.value`, `key`→`keyed()`,
  `.prop`/`?bool`/`@event`/`&ref` passed through as written, components become function calls,
  `{...props}` on elements needs `@verajs/renderer/spread`). Zero runtime
  cost via the Vite plugin; buildless stays the baseline, and `onClick=${fn}` works in raw
  templates too. **For a no-build app, see "Buildless JSX — the whole recipe" above.** JSX styles
  the templates only: components remain platform classes, so there are no hooks in function
  components. No decorators ever (they cannot run without a build step).
- **`computed` is `@verajs/store/computed`** (<!--size:computed.gzip-->238 B<!--/size:computed.gzip-->), not core. `computed(() => a + b)` evaluates once
    per change rather than once per read, and only when something it actually read moves. It is a
    store, so reading `.value` subscribes and computeds chain. The `'proxy-handler'` recipe in
    `examples/cdn-js/src/inserts/computed.js` remains a good insert example but does **not**
    memoise — it re-invokes on every read.

- **No Suspense, concurrent rendering, server components, or devtools.**
  Error boundaries: a worked example is `examples/cdn-js/src/inserts/error-boundary.js` (the
  `'error'` insert). Write batching/transactions: `examples/cdn-js/src/inserts/batch.js` (the
  `'set-handler'` insert).
- **No context/DI primitive.** Use a module-level store, or a `WeakMap` plus a DOM walk.
- **No `unsafeHTML`.** Interpolated values are escaped at the render boundary, always, and there is
  no sanctioned way to opt out — a rendering library is an XSS engine if it ships one, because the
  helper then appears in tutorials and code review reads it as blessed. If you genuinely have
  trusted markup, write the sink yourself as a property binding:

  ```js
  renderInto(html`<div .innerHTML=${trustedMarkup}></div>`, host);
  ```

  The friction is the feature. That line is greppable, obviously yours, and reviewable as the
  security decision it is. Sanitize before it — `DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` — unless the markup is
  genuinely your own. Note the renderer owns the element's children, so put the sink on an element
  whose content nothing else binds.
- **SSR is real and dependency-free**: `@verajs/ssr` renders components to declarative shadow
  DOM server-side (import it before core); `@verajs/renderer/hydrate` adopts the markup
  client-side. Comment-free server HTML; `keyed`/`hold` are client-only (use `.map` in SSR).

## Common mistakes

1. Defining a component before `setHtml` / `wire([renderer])` → with nothing on the `'render'`
   chain, `render()` warns once in development and draws nothing. (`mount()` is unaffected — it
   commits the setup and never reaches a renderer.)
2. Static `import` for components in the entry file → hoisted, same failure.
3. `wire(name, cb)` without a priority → ordering is undefined; always pass one. Registering at
   an **occupied** priority replaces that entry (this is how a renderer is swapped), and the
   replacement is named in a development warning.
4. `createStore` for large lists → use `shallowRef`.
5. Forgetting `init(this)` before `render` → nothing renders.
6. **Registering hooks and never committing the setup → none of them ever run.** `init()` opens a
   component's setup and one of two calls closes it: `render(template)` for a component with markup,
   `mount()` for one whose whole job is a side effect. Both run the first pass of every hook
   registered since `init()`. Development warns if neither happens, and names both.
7. Hooks after the setup is committed → ignored with a console warning. Register hooks between
   `init()` and the `render()` or `mount()` that closes it, or pass the element explicitly.
8. Expecting `useEffect` to run per mutation → it is coalesced; use `useSyncEffect`.
9. An autoloaded file that loads and defines a different tag than its name → reported via
   `vera:autoload-error` and the console; the module must define the element it is named for.
10. **TypeScript: a plain class field on a custom element silently destroys values set before the
   element upgrades.** Bound properties are repaired automatically (see *Props*), but a value
   assigned **imperatively** — `el.rows = data` before the definition loads — is gone for good.
   Use `declare`. See below; this one is invisible and costs you real data.
11. **`{cond && x}` in a TEMPLATE renders the word "false"** when `cond` is false — the value is
   not nullish, so it renders, exactly as lit does. Development names it. Write
   `${cond ? x : null}` or `${(cond && x) || null}`. **In JSX this is already handled** — a boolean
   child compiles away — which is the one value semantic where the two grammars differ.
12. **Passing an object to a component as an attribute.** `<x-rows rows=${data}>` in a template, or
   `rows={data}` on an **HTML** tag in JSX, is an *attribute* — always a string, so an array
   arrives as `"1,2,3"`. Bind a property: `.rows=${data}`, `props({ rows: data })`, or — on a
   dash-named tag in JSX — the bare `rows={data}`, which already means the property. Development
   names any non-primitive that reaches an attribute sink.
13. **TSX: forgetting `"types": ["@verajs/jsx"]`, or writing a sigil.** Without that tsconfig entry
   every element errors `TS7026` — the namespace ships with the plugin's declarations and a TSX app
   never imports the plugin. And `.date={d}` does not parse in `.tsx` (`TS1003`, TypeScript's own
   parser, before this plugin sees the file): write the bare prop, or `{...props({ date })}`.

## TypeScript: `declare` custom-element fields

```ts
class ChildElement extends HTMLElement {
  declare item?: { message: string };   // correct — emits nothing
  // item?: { message: string };        // emits `item;`, which runs during upgrade
}
```

**Bound properties no longer need this** — a component that calls `init()` has them re-applied
after upgrade (see *Props*, and both field spellings are repaired). `declare` is still the rule for
everything else, and still the safe habit, because of the one case nothing can recover: a property
assigned **imperatively** (`el.item = data`) before the element upgrades. Measured, all three:

```
.item=${…} bound, plain field, component calls init()  ->  value survives   (adopted and re-applied)
el.item = … imperative, plain field, init()            ->  value LOST       (the renderer never saw it)
el.item = … imperative, `declare item`                 ->  value survives   (no field to overwrite it)
```

At target ES2022 `useDefineForClassFields` is on, so a field *declaration* is a runtime
instruction: `item?: Thing` compiles to `item;`, which is
`Object.defineProperty(this, 'item', { value: undefined })`. Omitting the initializer does not
help; only `declare`, which emits nothing at all, does. Plain JavaScript is unaffected unless you
write `item = undefined` yourself.

That matters because a custom element is routinely given properties **before it upgrades** — a
parent binds `.item=${store}` while the child's module is still loading, or code assigns to an
element whose `customElements.define` has not run yet. The property lands on the un-upgraded
instance; then `define` upgrades it synchronously, the field initializer runs, and the value is
overwritten with `undefined`. Nothing throws. The component renders empty and the bug looks like
broken reactivity.

**What repairs it, and what cannot.** `@verajs/renderer` records every property binding nothing has
received yet, and `init()` re-applies the record after construction — unconditionally, so BOTH
spellings (`item;` and `item = someDefault`) resolve to the bound value: a bound value outranks a
class default, which is what props mean. That covers the common case completely and is why bound
props need no declaration of any kind.

It cannot cover a property assigned **imperatively**, because the renderer never saw it and class
fields initialise the instant `super()` returns — before the constructor body or
`connectedCallback` can look. For an element that never calls `init()`, nothing drains the record
either, so the clobber stands and `@verajs/renderer` **warns in development** (once per binding);
production carries neither the check nor the message.

`npx eslint` flags every plain class field on a custom element, if you use the config in this repo
— deliberately stricter than the repair, because nothing in the syntax says whether a field will be
written from outside, and the cost of being wrong is silent data loss against the cost of one
keyword.

All of the above is about a definition that arrives **late**. When the element is already defined
at render time, the binding goes through the class: the renderer stamps instances with
`importNode`, whose cloning steps upgrade defined elements at clone time, so a class **setter
fires** with the bound value (nothing shadows it) and a field initializer runs **before** the
commit, so the binding wins over the default — the same order hydration always had, since
server-rendered elements upgrade at parse. `declare` remains the safe habit because you do not
control when a consumer's module graph defines your element — but for BOUND properties the repair
above makes both orders agree, which is the point of it.

## Repository

- `packages/*` — the modules. `packages/*/dist/development/*.d.ts` is the source of truth for types.
- `docs/features/` — the differentiators, each with measurements and caveats.
- `docs/CODE-PRINCIPLES.md` — the bar every change must clear.
- `docs/RELEASING.md` — how releases are cut and published. Read before touching versions or `release.yml`.
- `bench/` — reactivity, bundle size and DOM benchmarks.
